draft.title: Measurement quality
card: Accuracy
How close a measurement is to the true value. Precision is how close repeated measurements are to each other.
Repeatability
the same person, using the same method and equipment, gets close results again. Reproducibility is when a different person or lab gets close results.
Resolution
the smallest change an instrument can show, such as 0.01 g on a balance. A smaller step means a finer resolution.
Validity
an investigation is valid when it measures what it claims to and controls other variables. Good results can still be invalid if the method tests the wrong thing.
draft.remember: Accuracy is closeness to the true value. Precision is closeness of repeats. Validity is whether the method tests the question.

a.q: Four titration results for a hydrochloric acid sample are 20.12, 20.14, 20.13 and 20.12 mL. The true value is 21.50 mL. How can the results be described?
a.why: The results are close to each other, so they are precise. They are all well away from 21.50 mL, so they are not accurate. Closeness of repeats does not show closeness to the true value.
a.clue: Compare the results to each other, then to the true value.

b.q: Priya measures the enthalpy of combustion of ethanol with a spirit burner and gets close results in three trials. Her teacher, using Priya's method, also gets close results to hers. Which quality does this show?
b.why: A different person using the same method gets close results, which is reproducibility. Repeatability is the same person repeating the work, which Priya did in her three trials. Close agreement alone does not show accuracy, because both could be far from the true value.
b.clue: Who obtained the second set of results?

problems.detail: The stem describes two things: Priya's three close trials, which show repeatability, and her teacher's matching results, which show reproducibility. 'Which quality does this show?' does not say which one is meant, so 'Repeatability of the results' is also defensible. Only the clue points to the teacher. The stem should ask what the teacher's results show.

check.summary: Question b is ambiguous. Priya's three close trials also show repeatability, so two options can be defended unless the stem asks only about the teacher's results. The card and question a are fine.

b.q: Priya measures the enthalpy of combustion of ethanol with a spirit burner. Her teacher then follows Priya's method and gets results close to hers. What does the teacher's agreement with Priya show?
b.why: A different person using the method gets close results, which is reproducibility. Repeatability would need the same person to repeat the work, but here the results come from two people. Close agreement alone does not show accuracy, because both could be far from the true value.
b.clue: Are the two sets of results from the same person?
